name: Bhawani Amba Temple Ambala
description: Located in the heart of old Ambala City, an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Bhawani Amba (Mata Ambika), from whom the historic city of Ambala derives its name, revered for centuries by rulers and citizens as the protector goddess of the region, featuring an ancient sanctum, decorative silver shikhara, and bustling Navratri celebrations.

name: Gurudwara Panjokhara Sahib Ambala
description: Situated 8 km from Ambala on the Ambala-Naraingarh road, the historic gurudwara where the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan Ji (aged seven), stayed in 1664 on his way to Delhi, renowned for the miracle where the child Guru bestowed profound spiritual wisdom upon an illiterate village deaf-mute water carrier Chhajju Ram, who then recited deep philosophical commentaries on the Bhagavad Gita to humble the proud scholar Pandit Lal Chand.

name: Fort of Loharu & Rawatsar Haveli
description: Constructed in 1570 CE by Thakur Arjun Singh and later seat of the princely State of Loharu under Nawab Ahmad Baksh Khan, a historic mud-and-stone fortress with royal baradaris, sheesh mahal rooms, and arched gateways, culturally renowned as the ancestral home of Nawabzada Mirza Ghalib's wife Umrao Begum and Urdu literary patron Nawab Ziauddin Ahmad Khan.

name: Star Monument Bhiwani (Tara Maqbara)
description: Situated 12 km from Bhiwani at Dinod village, an astonishing hexagonal six-pointed star-shaped marble monument rising 88 feet, built to enshrine the samadhi of spiritual master Param Sant Huzur Tara Chand Ji Maharaj (Bade Maharaj Ji), engineered without a single supporting pillar or column using innovative geometric cantilevered architecture, surrounded by lush landscaped star-patterned fountains.

name: Tosham Hill & Rock Inscriptions
description: Rising 800 feet abruptly from the flat plains of Bhiwani, an isolated igneous rocky hill featuring historic 5th-century CE Sanskrit rock inscriptions carved on vertical basalt faces documenting the lineage of Acharya Somatrata, rock-cut water reservoirs (kunds) built by Prithviraj Chauhan, and ancient temples dedicated to Baba Mungipa and Lord Vishnu.

name: Palace of Dadri (Charkhi Dadri Fort)
description: Built in the 18th century by the Phulkian rulers of Jind State on a high mound in Charkhi Dadri, a stately brick and stone palace-fortress featuring high defensive ramparts, ornamental wooden balconies, royal darbar courtyards, and ancient cenotaphs, associated with Dadri's legendary folk wrestling and Rajput valor.

name: Anangpur Dam
description: Constructed in the 8th century CE during the reign of King Anangpal I of the Tomar dynasty near Anangpur village, an extraordinary ancient hydraulic engineering marvel consisting of a 50-meter-wide gravity dam built of massive quartzite stone blocks, designed to trap rain torrents flowing through an Aravalli gully into a stepped reservoir.

name: Ancient Site of Tilpat (Tilaprastha of Mahabharata)
description: Situated near the Yamuna River in northern Faridabad, an ancient archaeological mound identified with 'Tilaprastha', one of the five historic villages (along with Indraprastha, Paniprastha, Sonaprastha, and Baghpat) demanded by Yudhishthira from Duryodhana to avert the catastrophic Mahabharata war, excavated by ASI to reveal Painted Grey Ware (PGW) dating to 1000 BCE.

name: Badkhal Lake & Eco-Restoration Promenade
description: Constructed in 1947 shortly after independence by building an earthen bund between two Aravalli hill ridges to hold rainwater runoff, an iconic recreational lake in Faridabad undergoing comprehensive ecological rejuvenation with a modern lakefront promenade, boating jetties, and lush tree plantations.

name: Mangar Bani Sacred Grove & Palaeolithic Aravallis
description: Nestled in a pristine Aravalli valley bordering Gurugram and Faridabad, an ancient 677-acre climax virgin forest dominated by pure stands of Dhau trees (Anogeissus pendula), preserved for centuries by local Gujjar villagers under the sacred protection of hermit Gudariya Baba, discovered in 2021 as the largest Stone Age Palaeolithic cave and stone-tool factory in the Indian subcontinent dating back 100,000 years.

name: Raja Nahar Singh Palace Ballabgarh
description: Constructed in 1739 CE by Rao Balram and embellished by the 1857 martyr Raja Nahar Singh, an imposing double-storeyed Jat palace featuring ornamental sand-cast battlements, intricate cusped archways, a Darbar Hall, carved jharokhas, and a dazzling Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), converted by Haryana Tourism into a heritage palace hotel.

name: Surajkund & Ancient Sun Temple Ruins
description: Built in the 10th century CE by King Suraj Pal of the Tomar dynasty who worshiped the Sun God, a monumental semicircular stepped stone amphitheatre (Pool of the Sun) backed by the Aravalli hills, engineered to collect torrential rainwater runoff from the surrounding rocky catchment, famous globally for hosting the annual Surajkund International Crafts Mela in February.

name: Banawali Harappan Archaeological Site
description: Situated on the dried bed of the ancient sacred Saraswati River in Fatehabad district, an exceptional fortified Harappan city excavated by Dr. R. S. Bisht of the ASI, internationally noted for its unique radial street planning (unlike the typical gridiron), pre-Harappan defensive ramparts, terracotta plough models confirming early agriculture, and a lapidary bead factory.

name: Bhirrana Archaeological Site
description: Located on the banks of the dried palaeochannel of the Saraswati River, recognized by carbon-14 radiometric dating by IIT Kharagpur and ASI as the oldest Indus Valley / Saraswati Civilization settlement discovered in the Indian subcontinent, with cultural strata extending from the pre-Harappan Hakra phase (7500-6000 BCE) continuously through the mature Harappan period.

name: Kunal Archaeological Site
description: Situated on the dried bed of the Saraswati River in Ratia tehsil, a vital early Harappan Hakra ware archaeological site excavated by the Haryana Department of Archaeology, famous for the discovery of two royal silver diadems (crowns), 12,000 micro-beads, and gold ornaments proving the existence of an organized royal elite before the mature Harappan phase.

name: Badshahpur Fort & Baoli Gurugram
description: Situated in Badshahpur in southern Gurugram, a historic 18th-century stone-and-brick fort and multi-storeyed arched stepwell (baoli) associated with the legendary warrior-queen Begum Samru of Sardhana, featuring arched galleries, subterranean chambers, and defensive gateways that guarded the southern trade route to Delhi.

name: Damdama Lake & Adventure Valley
description: Formed in 1947 by the British by commissioning an earthen embankment to harvest rainwater in a hollow between ancient Aravalli ridges, the largest natural lake in Haryana covering over 3,000 acres, famed for row and paddle boating, adventure camping, ziplining, rock climbing on natural Aravalli crags, and winter migratory birdwatching.

name: DLF CyberHub Gurugram
description: Spanning 200,000 square feet in the heart of Gurugram's corporate cyber city, India's premier integrated social, dining, and retail promenade, housing over 80 gourmet restaurants, microbreweries, and an open amphitheatre.

name: Farrukhnagar
description: Farrukhnagar, a historic town in Haryana's Gurugram district, presents a captivating blend of Mughal-era heritage and the rustic beauty of the Aravalli foothills. Founded in 1732 by Faujdar Khan, the first Nawab, the town was named after Emperor Farrukhsiyar and still boasts impressive structures from its past. While primarily celebrated for its architectural marvels like the exquisite Sheesh Mahal and a magnificent stepwell, Farrukhnagar also serves as a gateway to explore the surrounding semi-arid natural landscape. The local culture is deeply rooted in traditional Haryanvi life, with a strong agricultural base, providing visitors an authentic glimpse into rural customs, cuisine, and the unhurried pace of the countryside. Its strategic location at the edge of the Aravallis allows for unique opportunities to connect with nature and engage in outdoor activities beyond its historical core.

name: Leisure Valley Park Gurugram
description: A 25-acre landscaped urban green park in the heart of millennium city Gurugram, featuring jogging tracks, musical fountains, a rose garden, and open-air concert grounds adjacent to the Kingdom of Dreams.

name: Museo Camera Centre for Photographic Arts
description: Established as a unique public-private partnership between photographer Aditya Arya and the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram across 18,000 square feet, the largest non-profit museum dedicated to photography in South Asia, displaying over 2,500 vintage cameras from the 1850s to the 1990s, original daguerreotypes, darkrooms, and contemporary photo art galleries.

name: Sheetala Mata Temple Gurugram
description: Located in the heart of old Gurugram (the ancient village of Guru Dronacharya), an immensely revered Hindu pilgrimage shrine dedicated to Mata Sheetala Devi (Mata Kripi, wife of Dronacharya, revered for curing smallpox, measles, and childhood diseases), attracting millions of devotees especially for children's first hair-cleansing ceremonies (mundan).

name: Sohna Sulphur Hot Springs & Shiva Temple
description: Perched at the foot of the Aravalli hills in Sohna, natural volcanic thermal sulphur springs that bubble out of the ground at a steady temperature between 46°C and 51°C, celebrated since Vedic times for their therapeutic and medicinal properties that cure skin diseases, arthritis, and rheumatism, featuring indoor bath cubicles and an ancient Shiva temple.

name: Sultanpur National Park
description: A designated Ramsar wetland and national park spread over 350 acres of freshwater marshes, serving as one of Northern India's premier birdwatching havens hosting over 250 bird species including Siberian cranes and flamingos.

name: Tau Devi Lal Biodiversity Park Gurugram
description: Spread across 32 lush green acres in Sector 52 of Gurugram, developed by the Haryana Urban Development Authority as the city's premier green lung and urban biodiversity park, featuring over 150 species of native Aravalli trees, medicinal plant gardens, butterfly zones, and a world-class 1-kilometer cushioned clay jogging track.

name: Ancient Mound Agroha & Agroha Dham
description: Sprawling across 650 acres on the National Highway 20 km from Hisar, the ancient capital of the legendary King Agrasen of the Agroha Republic mentioned in the Mahabharata, featuring an ASI-excavated 87-foot-high archaeological mound revealing ancient Buddhist stupas, Roman coins, and terracotta plaques, complemented by the grand modern red-and-white marble temple complex of Agroha Dham.

name: Asigarh Fort Hansi (Fort of Prithviraj Chauhan)
description: Perched on a high archaeological mound in Hansi dating back to the Kushan era, reconstructed in the 12th century by Rajput Emperor Prithviraj Chauhan to secure the frontier against invasions, famous for its 30-acre ramparts, 1303 CE Sultanate Barsi Gate with intricate Arabic inscriptions, and George Thomas's 18th-century royal mint.

name: Blue Bird Lake & Tourist Complex Hisar
description: Spanning 52 acres on National Highway 9 near Hisar, a scenic artificial lake and wetland park operated by Haryana Tourism, featuring boating, a floating restaurant, walking tracks, and seasonal marshlands that attract over 100 species of winter migratory waterfowl from Siberia.

name: Dargah Char Qutab Hansi
description: A magnificent 800-year-old Sufi pilgrimage complex in Hansi enshrining four legendary Chishti Sufi mystics (Qutabs: Jamal-ud-din Hanswi, Burhan-ud-din, Qutb-ud-din Munawwar, and Nur-ud-din), featuring a monumental red-sandstone mosque built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq, domed pavilions, and centuries of syncretic spiritual reverence.

name: Firoz Shah Palace & Lat Ki Masjid Hisar
description: Constructed in 1354 CE by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq as the fortified citadel of 'Hisar-e-Firoza', built of massive rubble stone and lime mortar, featuring extensive underground cool subterranean chambers (Tahkhanas), the Lat Ki Masjid with a 3rd-century BCE polished sandstone Ashokan pillar shaft, and an intricate stepwell (Baoli).

name: Gujari Mahal Hisar
description: Constructed in 1356 CE by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq for his beloved tribal Gujar peasant consort Gujari who refused to leave her native land for Delhi, a striking two-storey palace built on a high stone plinth outside the fort walls, featuring nine grand domes, open pavilions (baradaris), and underground living chambers.

name: Rakhigarhi Archaeological Site & National Museum
description: Spanning over 350 hectares across seven massive mounds in the ancient Drishadvati river basin, officially proven to be the largest city of the Harappan / Indus Valley Civilization (surpassing Mohenjo-daro and Harappa in size), continuously inhabited from 5500 BCE to 1900 BCE, featuring planned mud-brick grid streets, covered drainage networks, lapidary workshops, and a state-of-the-art National Archaeological Site Museum.

name: Bhimeshwari Devi Temple Beri (Beri Wali Mata)
description: Situated in Beri town 15 km from Jhajjar, an immensely revered Shakti shrine dedicated to Goddess Bhimeshwari Devi, believed to have been installed by Pandava warrior Bhima while returning from the Hinglaj Shakti Peetha with the idol of the Goddess before the Kurukshetra war, featuring dual sanctums and monumental Navratri fairs attracting millions of devotees.

name: Bhindawas Wildlife Sanctuary & Lake
description: Designated as a Ramsar Site of International Importance in 2021 spanning 1,016 acres of freshwater wetland and lake surrounded by a 12-kilometer earthen embankment, the largest human-made wetland in Haryana, hosting over 250 species of birds and more than 30,000 winter migratory waterfowl including painted storks, bar-headed geese, and sarus cranes.

name: Gurukul Jhajjar Archaeological Museum
description: Founded in 1959 by Swami Omanand Saraswati within the historic Gurukul Jhajjar campus, the largest private archaeological and numismatic museum in Haryana, holding over 200,000 ancient artifacts including rare Indus Valley terracotta seals, Gupta and Kushan coins, ancient bronze sculptures, medieval weapons, and handwritten palm-leaf manuscripts.

name: Khaparwas Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Covering 204 acres of shallow freshwater marshland and reeds in Jhajjar district just 1.5 km from the Bhindawas Ramsar site, a tranquil avian sanctuary attracting thousands of migratory waterfowl including bar-headed geese, shovelers, common teals, and sarus cranes.

name: Pratapgarh Farms Jhajjar
description: Set across sprawling agricultural acres in Gwalison village near Jhajjar, an acclaimed ethnic rural holiday resort and cultural village offering complete immersion in traditional Haryanvi and Rajasthani rural life, featuring authentic mud cottages, pottery making, camel and tractor rides, folk dances (Ghoomar, Been-Jogi), and unlimited traditional culinary feasting.

name: Dhamtan Sahib Gurudwara
description: Located in Dhamtan village near Narwana, a monumental historic gurudwara built like a walled fortress with massive bastions, commemorating the visit of the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who stayed here with his disciples in 1675 on his way to Delhi before his supreme martyrdom at Chandni Chowk, also associated with the Vedic hermitage of Sage Valmiki.

name: Jayanti Devi Temple & Fort of Jind
description: The historic origin of Jind town (ancient Jaintapuri), established by the Pandavas who erected a temple to Goddess Jayanti (Goddess of Victory) to seek blessings before the battle of Kurukshetra, complemented by the 18th-century royal fortress of Jind and the picturesque Rani Talab lake with its central Shiva temple (Bhuteshwar Temple) built by Raja Raghbir Singh in the late 19th century.

name: Pandu Pindara Tirth
description: Located 6 km from Jind, an immensely sacred water tank (Pindar Tirth) where according to the Mahabharata the Pandavas spent 12 long years waiting for Somavati Amavasya (no-moon day falling on a Monday) to perform the salvation rites and Pinda Daan for their slain relatives and soldiers following the catastrophic 18-day Kurukshetra war.

name: Safidon Nag Kshetra Tirth
description: Anciently known as Sarpadevi, the historic holy city where King Janamejaya (son of Parikshit and great-grandson of Arjuna) performed the colossal Sarpa Satra snake-sacrifice yajna to avenge his father's death by the serpent Takshaka, featuring the sacred stepped tank of Nag Kshetra and the ancient Nageshwar Mahadev Temple.

name: Saraswati Wildlife Sanctuary (Seonsar Forest)
description: Spanning 11,000 acres (4,482 hectares) across Kaithal and Kurukshetra districts along the ancient dried bed of the Saraswati River, the third largest forest reserve in Haryana, renowned for its dense canopy of Kikar and Dhak (Flame of the Forest) trees sheltering leopards, nilgai, wild boars, rhesus macaques, and Indian peafowls.

name: Tomb of Razia Sultan Kaithal
description: Situated in a peaceful walled enclosure near the Siwan Gate in Kaithal, the historical brick-and-mortar tomb marking the burial place of Jalalat-ud-Din Razia (Razia Sultan), the first and only woman monarch to rule the throne of Delhi, who was defeated and assassinated here along with her husband Malik Altunia on 14 October 1240 CE.

name: Kalpana Chawla Memorial Planetarium Karnal
description: Constructed by the Haryana Department of Science and Technology in Karnal (the birthplace of astronaut Kalpana Chawla), a futuristic planetarium and space science museum featuring a full-dome digital planetarium, life-sized scale models of space shuttles and satellites, and an inspirational exhibition gallery tracing Kalpana's life journey from Karnal to NASA.

name: Karna Lake Tourist Resort Karnal
description: Located alongside National Highway 44 near Karnal (named after Raja Karna of Mahabharata fame), a serene recreational lake and flagship Haryana Tourism resort complex surrounded by lush gardens, where King Karna is believed to have bathed and donated his impenetrable golden armor (Kavach and Kundal) to Lord Indra in charity.

name: Ancient Mound Amin (Abhimanyu's Chakravyuha Site)
description: Located in Amin village 8 km from Kurukshetra, an ancient 60-foot-high archaeological mound traditionally identified with the site of the lethal multi-tiered Chakravyuha battle formation where 16-year-old warrior Abhimanyu (son of Arjuna) was trapped and valiantly attained martyrdom on the 13th day of the Mahabharata war.

name: Bhishma Kund Narkatari
description: Situated in Narkatari village 5 km from Thanesar, the historic battlefield site where the patriarch Bhishma Pitamah lay on a bed of arrows (Sharsaiyya) awaiting Uttarayana, where Arjuna shot a celestial arrow into the earth to unleash a fresh geyser spring of holy Ganga water to quench his dying grandfather's thirst.

name: Birla Gita Mandir Kurukshetra
description: Constructed in 1952 by industrialist Jugal Kishore Birla, a magnificent white marble temple dedicated to Lord Krishna and Arjuna, featuring all 18 chapters and 700 verses of the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita meticulously engraved in Devanagari script along its interior marble walls, fronted by a monumental bronze chariot driven by four horses.

name: Brahma Sarovar Kurukshetra
description: One of the largest man-made water tanks in Asia measuring 3,600 feet long and 1,500 feet wide, dedicated to Lord Brahma who is believed to have created the universe from this spot, mentioned by Mughal court historian Abul Fazl in Ain-i-Akbari as 'the miniature sea', and epicentre of solar eclipse sacred dips attracting over a million pilgrims.

name: Chhilchhila Wildlife Sanctuary Pehowa
description: Covering 71 acres around an ancient depression on the Saraswati river plain near Pehowa, a vital protected bird wetland designated in 1986, celebrated as a crucial breeding and wintering refuge for over 4,000 birds and 29 species of waterfowl, including the vulnerable Indian Spot-billed Duck, Gadwall, and Northern Pintail.

name: Dharohar Museum Kurukshetra University
description: Established within the lush green campus of Kurukshetra University, a premier folk and ethnographic living heritage museum spanning multiple galleries that meticulously recreates the traditional rural lifestyle, architecture, crafts, cattle shelters, traditional attire, and folk musical instruments of authentic rural Haryana.

name: Jyotisar (Birthplace of the Bhagavad Gita)
description: The venerated ground where Lord Krishna delivered the celestial song of the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita to the despondent warrior Arjuna at the commencement of the 18-day Mahabharata war, anchored by an offshoot of the immortal 5,000-year-old banyan tree (Akshay Vat) that bore witness to the celestial sermon.

name: Kurukshetra Panorama and Science Centre
description: Inaugurated in 2001 adjacent to Brahma Sarovar by the National Council of Science Museums, featuring a colossal 34-foot-high cylindrical auditorium with a 360-degree lifelike three-dimensional panoramic painting and diorama depicting the 18-day epic Mahabharata war with authentic battlefield sound and lighting effects, alongside hands-on science galleries exploring ancient Indian scientific heritage.

name: Maa Bhadrakali Temple Kurukshetra
description: Recognized as one of the 51 ancient Shakti Peethas of Goddess Sati, where according to Hindu mythology the right ankle of Sati fell during Shiva's cosmic dance of destruction, and where the Pandavas offered black royal horses to Goddess Bhadrakali after emerging victorious in the Mahabharata war.

name: Mahabharata Anubhav Kendra & Light-and-Sound Complex
description: A state-of-the-art experiential multimedia museum complex developed by Haryana Tourism and the Ministry of Tourism under the Krishna Circuit at Jyotisar, utilizing augmented reality, 3D holographic projections, animatronic installations, and digital storytelling to immerse visitors in the events, philosophy, and characters of the Mahabharata.

name: Prithudak Tirth Pehowa
description: Situated on the banks of the sacred Saraswati River 27 km from Kurukshetra, named after legendary King Prithu who performed shraddha rites for his father King Vena here, revered across northern India on par with Gaya for performing ancestral Pinda Daan and Tarpan rituals, featuring the ancient Saraswati Temple and Kartikeya Temple.

name: Sannihit Sarovar Kurukshetra
description: Measuring 1,500 feet by 450 feet, revered as the confluence point of the seven sacred streams of the ancient Saraswati River and the cosmic abode of Lord Vishnu, believed to hold the sanctity of all pilgrimages combined during solar eclipses and Amavasya days.

name: Sheikh Chilli's Tomb & Madrasa
description: Constructed in 1650 CE atop an archaeological mound in Thanesar, an exquisite Mughal octagonal mausoleum built of pure white marble over a sandstone terrace, enshrining the Sufi saint Abd-ur-Rahim (popularly known as Sheikh Chilli, spiritual mentor of Mughal prince Dara Shikoh), featuring a pear-shaped dome, charbagh gardens, and an adjacent red sandstone madrasa and ASI archaeological museum.

name: Sthaneshwar Mahadev Temple
description: The presiding deity temple of Thanesar (historically Sthanishvara, capital of Emperor Harshavardhana in the 7th century), housing an ancient self-manifested Shiva Lingam worshiped by the Pandavas in the presence of Lord Krishna before the Kurukshetra war to secure victory, complemented by a sacred water tank with healing powers.

name: Birbal Ka Chhatta Narnaul
description: Constructed during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan by Ray-i-Rayan Rai Bal Mukund Das (Diwan of Narnaul), a monumental five-storeyed red stone mansion (haveli) featuring three underground basement levels (tahkhanas) with skylights, subterranean water conduits, marble courtyards, and ornate jharokhas, popularly associated with Akbar's wazir Birbal.

name: Chor Gumbad Narnaul
description: Standing proudly on an isolated rocky outcrop overlooking Narnaul, an impressive square Afghan-style tomb constructed by Afghan nobleman Jamal Khan during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, featuring four corner minaret-style towers, twenty arched openings, and a massive central dome, historically known as 'Chor Gumbad' (Thieves' Dome) because desert bandits used it as a hideout.

name: Dhosi Hill (Vedic Chyavan Rishi Ashram)
description: Rising to 2,430 feet on the Haryana-Rajasthan border, an isolated extinct volcanic hill featuring a prominent crater lake at the summit, famous in Vedic antiquity as the hermitage of Sage Chyavana who formulated the legendary Ayurvedic health formulation 'Chyavanprash' here using wild Amla and forest herbs, featuring ancient Shiva temples, stepped pathways, and volcanic sulfur vents.

name: Jal Mahal Narnaul
description: Constructed in 1591 CE by Shah Quli Khan (governor of Narnaul who captured Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat), a stunning floating pleasure water palace set squarely in the middle of a massive 11-acre artificial lake (Khan Sarovar), accessible via an ornate arched causeway with 16 fluted pillars and domed corner kiosks (chhatris).

name: Tomb of Ibrahim Khan Suri Narnaul
description: Constructed in 1540 CE by Emperor Sher Shah Suri (founder of the Sur Empire) over the grave of his grandfather Ibrahim Khan Suri who was a military jagirdar in Narnaul, an architectural masterpiece of the Sur / Pathan style built of square grey sandstone blocks, featuring carved red stone brackets, deep arched recesses, and a lofty dome.

name: Tripolia Gateway & Tomb of Shah Wilayat
description: Constructed in 1589 CE by Shah Quli Khan in Narnaul, the monumental 'Tripolia Gateway' built of red and grey sandstone leading to the serene tomb complex of 14th-century Sufi saint Hazrat Shah Wilayat, featuring exquisite Islamic calligraphy, painted floral arabesques, and tranquil courtyards.

name: Heritage Transport Museum Taoru
description: Spread over 90,000 square feet across four multi-tiered air-conditioned galleries in Taoru near Gurugram, India's first and only comprehensive transport museum, showcasing over 2,500 curated artifacts chronicling the evolution of transportation in India, including vintage cars, steam locomotives, restored railway saloons, antique palanquins, vintage aircraft, and tribal bullock carts.

name: Gandhi Ashram & Historical Railway Station Palwal
description: Situated at the historic Palwal Railway Station and Gandhi Seva Ashram, an indelible national heritage monument commemorating 10 April 1919, when Mahatma Gandhi was arrested on Indian soil for the very first time by the British while traveling to Punjab to oppose the draconian Rowlatt Act, featuring a memorial pillar, museum, and spinning charkha gallery inaugurated by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose in 1938.

name: Panchvati Temple Palwal
description: Situated in the ancient holy city of Palwal (associated with demon Palwasura slain by Balarama), a revered temple nestled within five sacred banyan trees (Panch Vata) where the Pandavas are believed to have spent part of their 12-year exile (Vanvas) in meditation, featuring an ancient stepped kund and shrines dedicated to Lord Krishna, Shiva, and Hanuman.

name: Bhima Devi Temple Complex Pinjore
description: Dating from the 8th to the 11th century CE during the Gurjara-Pratihara empire, a magnificent Panchayatana-style stone temple complex and open-air sculpture museum located just 500 meters from Pinjore Gardens, widely hailed as the 'Khajuraho of North India' for its hundreds of exquisitely carved sandstone sculptures of celestial apsaras, deities, musicians, and erotic mithuna couples.

name: Bir Shikargah Wildlife Sanctuary Pinjore
description: Covering 1,893 acres of deciduous Shivalik foothill forest near Pinjore, originally the royal hunting preserve of the Maharaja of Patiala, home to leopards, sambar, barking deer, wild boars, and the internationally celebrated Jatayu Vulture Conservation Breeding Centre (VCBC), Asia's premier facility dedicated to saving critically endangered Indian vulture species from extinction.

name: Khol Hi-Raitan Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Spanning 12,000 acres (4,883 hectares) of rugged Shivalik foothill forest contiguous with Bir Shikargah and the Morni Hills, a crucial ecological corridor for leopards, Indian gaurs, sambar, barking deer, wild boars, and jungle cats, featuring deep ravines, seasonal waterholes, and dense chir pine and bamboo canopies.

name: Mata Mansa Devi Temple Panchkula
description: Nestled in the scenic Shivalik foothills of Bilaspur village near Panchkula, constructed between 1811 and 1815 CE by Maharaja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra, an extraordinarily revered Shakti shrine dedicated to Goddess Mansa Devi (an incarnation of Durga who fulfills all wishes), featuring 38 miniature wall frescoes and grand nine-day Navratri fairs drawing over a million pilgrims.

name: Morni Hills
description: Perched amidst the lush Shivalik range in Haryana, the picturesque Morni Hills offers a respite from the urban chaos. This lesser-explored destination is a haven for nature enthusiasts, photographers, and adventure seekers. The hill station boasts of lush forests, scenic valleys, and rolling hills that beckon visitors to indulge in a range of activities. As you wander through the misty forests, listen to the sweet melodies of birds and breathe in the crisp mountain air, you'll begin to unravel the charms of this hidden gem. The perfect blend of natural beauty, rich history, and thrilling experiences makes Morni Hills a must-visit destination for those seeking an offbeat escape.

name: Nada Sahib Gurudwara Panchkula
description: Situated on the banks of the Ghaggar River against the backdrop of the Shivalik hills, the historical gurudwara where the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh Ji, halted with his victorious army in 1688 after the Battle of Bhangani, welcomed and served with deep devotion by local disciple Nadu Shah Lubana.

name: National Cactus and Succulent Botanical Garden
description: Established in 1987 in Sector 5 of Panchkula by noted botanist Dr. J. S. Sarkaria across 7 acres, recognized as the largest outdoor cactus and succulent botanical garden in Asia, dedicated to conserving endangered desert flora and housing over 3,500 rare species of cacti and succulents from the Americas, Africa, and India, including giant columnar Carnegias and medicinal Aloes.

name: Tikkar Taal
description: Tikkar Taal, comprising two picturesque lakes known as Big Tikkar and Small Tikkar, is a hidden gem tucked away in the lower Shivalik ranges of the Morni Hills in Haryana's Panchkula district. This peaceful village destination offers a refreshing escape from urban life, characterized by its lush green surroundings, diverse avian life, and gentle rolling hills. The local culture here is deeply intertwined with the natural landscape, with villagers often engaged in agriculture and maintaining a close-knit community spirit. It's a place where time slows down, allowing visitors to connect with pristine nature and experience authentic rural Haryanvi hospitality, making it ideal for those seeking tranquility and natural beauty away from the bustling city.

name: Yadavindra Gardens (Pinjore Gardens)
description: Created in the 17th century by Nawab Fidai Khan (architect brother of Emperor Aurangzeb), a magnificent 100-acre terraced garden featuring seven descending canal terraces, Shish Mahal, Rang Mahal, and illuminated fountains.

name: Dargah of Bu-Ali-Shah Qalandar
description: Built in the early 14th century in red sandstone by Mahabat Khan (general of Mughal Emperor Jahangir), enshrining the 13th-century Sufi saint and poet Sheikh Sharaf-ud-din Bu-Ali-Shah Qalandar, revered by devotees across northern India for unity, communal harmony, and ecstatic Thursday Qawwali sessions.

name: Ibrahim Lodhi's Tomb Panipat
description: Situated near the tehsil office in Panipat, a dignified rectangular red stone tomb set upon a high brick platform with arched niches, marking the burial place of Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi, the last ruler of the Lodhi Dynasty and the Delhi Sultanate, who was killed on 21 April 1526 in the First Battle of Panipat against Babur.

name: Kabuli Bagh Mosque Panipat
description: Constructed in 1526 CE by the first Mughal Emperor Babur to commemorate his decisive victory over Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat, celebrated as the very first Mughal architectural monument erected in India, named after Babur's wife Kabuli Begum, featuring a grand central dome, prayer hall with Persian inscriptions, and charbagh gardens.

name: Kala Amb & Third Battle of Panipat Memorial
description: Marked by a black stone obelisk pillar amidst a landscaped park, the historic epicenter of the fateful Third Battle of Panipat fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire under Sadashivrao Bhau and the Afghan forces of Ahmad Shah Durrani, named after a giant black mango tree (Kala Amb) under which Sadashivrao Bhau made his heroic final stand.

name: Panipat Battle Museum & Memorial
description: Established by the Panipat Historical Society and Haryana Tourism, a specialized military museum dedicated exclusively to the history, armaments, military tactics, and artifacts of the three world-changing Battles of Panipat (1526, 1556, and 1761), exhibiting authentic medieval armor, matchlock guns, swords, maps, miniature paintings, and dioramas.

name: Bada Talab (Rao Tej Singh Talab) Rewari
description: Constructed between 1810 and 1815 CE by Rao Tej Singh of the Rewari royal dynasty, an imposing sandstone stepped water reservoir measuring over 200 feet on each side, equipped with intricate underground inlet channels, decorative chhatris, bathing ghats for women, and an adjacent historic Hanuman Mandir.

name: Fort of Bawal Rewari
description: Constructed in the 18th century by Raja Sawai Hira Singh of the princely Phulkian Nabha State, a sturdy rectangular brick and stone fortress featuring high crenellated battlements, massive circular corner bastions, royal baradaris, and a historic stepwell, serving as the southern administrative seat of Nabha rulers.

name: Nahar Wildlife Sanctuary Kosli
description: Spanning 522 acres of mixed deciduous thorn and scrub woodland in Kosli taluka of Rewari district, originally preserved as the private royal pasture of the Nawab of Dujana, officially designated as a wildlife sanctuary in 1987 to protect wild populations of Indian Blackbuck, monitor lizards, jackals, and desert foxes.

name: Rewari Railway Heritage Museum & Steam Shed
description: Constructed in 1893 on the Delhi-Rewari metre gauge line, the only operational steam locomotive shed remaining in India, revitalized in 2002 by Indian Railways as a premier national railway heritage museum, housing 11 operational vintage broad-gauge and metre-gauge steam engines, including the legendary 1855 'Fairy Queen' (Guinness World Record holder as the world's oldest working steam locomotive) and the 1953 'Akbar'.

name: Farmana Archaeological Site (Daksh Khera)
description: Spanning 18.5 hectares in the Yamuna-Ghaggar interfluve, excavated jointly by the Maharshi Dayanand University and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (Japan), famous for uncovering 70 Harappan skeletons in the largest burial ground of the Indus Valley Civilization in Haryana, complete with organized residential blocks, copper bangles, steatite seals, and carbonized botanical seeds.

name: Khokhrakot Mound Rohtak
description: Sprawling across a 50-foot-high archaeological mound in Rohtak city, the ancient capital of Rohitaka mentioned in the Mahabharata's Sabhaparva as conquered by Nakula, and capital of the martial Yaudheya Republic (2nd century BCE to 4th century CE), famous for unearthing thousands of Yaudheya coin moulds, Kushan seals, and terracotta figurines.

name: Tilyar Lake
description: Tilyar Lake, a prominent tourist complex managed by Haryana Tourism, is nestled near the city of Rohtak. This man-made lake is a beloved recreational hub, renowned for its lush green surroundings, calm waters, and family-friendly amenities. While Haryana is largely characterized by its flat plains, Tilyar Lake provides a refreshing natural escape, attracting both locals and tourists seeking a peaceful retreat from urban life. It has evolved into a significant leisure destination, offering a blend of natural tranquility and recreational activities. The geographical setting of Tilyar Lake is defined by its expansive water body surrounded by well-maintained gardens and open spaces, making it an ideal spot for picnics and leisurely strolls. The local experience revolves around enjoying the outdoors, with opportunities for boating, wildlife observation, and simply relaxing amidst nature. The complex also houses a mini zoo, further enhancing its appeal as a wholesome family destination where visitors can connect with the local flora and fauna.

name: Abubshahar Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Sprawling across 28,400 acres (115 sq km) near Mandi Dabwali in the extreme western corner of Haryana bordering Punjab and Rajasthan, a massive open acacia-scrub and sand-dune wildlife sanctuary sheltering the largest wild population of Blackbuck antelopes in the state, alongside chinkara, desert foxes, and blue bulls.

name: Dera Baba Sarsai Nath Sirsa
description: Constructed in the 13th century by Saint Sarsai Nath of the Kanphata Nath yogi tradition (from whom Sirsa derives its ancient name 'Sarsuti'), an immensely venerated spiritual monastic complex featuring ancient Shiva temples, a continuous eternal sacred fire (Dhuni), and historical relics documenting visits by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.

name: Ther Mound Sirsa
description: Covering over 80 acres and rising to a height of 50 feet in Sirsa town, a colossal archaeological citadel mound overlooking the dry valley of the Ghaggar-Saraswati River, excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India to reveal continuous human occupation spanning 1,500 years from the early historic Rang Mahal culture to the medieval Sultanate era.

name: Murthal Culinary Heritage Highway
description: Situated on National Highway 44 (the historic Sher Shah Suri Marg / Grand Trunk Road) 50 km north of Delhi, world-famous as the ultimate culinary pilgrimage corridor of North India, home to legendary round-the-clock dhabas (Amrik Sukhdev, Gulshan, Pahalwan, Mannat) renowned for piping-hot tandoori stuffed paranthas served with massive dollops of homemade white butter (safed makkhan).

name: Tomb of Khwaja Khizr Sonipat
description: Constructed in 1522-1524 CE by Langar Khan during the reign of Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi, a masterwork of late Delhi Sultanate Pathan architecture built of dressed red sandstone and kankar blocks on a high stone terrace, enshrining local saint Khwaja Khizr, featuring an ornamental arched gateway with Arabic calligraphy and a fluted dome.

name: Adi Badri & Saraswati Udgam Sthal
description: Perched at an elevation of 1,000 meters in the dense sal forests of the Shivalik foothills on the Haryana-Himachal border, revered as the sacred origin point (Udgam Sthal) where the Vedic Saraswati River descends from the Himalayas into the plains, home to the ancient Adi Badri Narayana Temple, Kedar Temple, and archaeological remains dating to the Buddhist and Gurjara-Pratihara eras.

name: Ancient Site of Sugh (Srughna) & Topra Ashokan Pillar Site
description: Covering a massive archaeological mound on the old bed of the Yamuna River, the ancient metropolis of Srughna (Sugh) mentioned by Panini, Patanjali, and Xuanzang as a flourishing centre of Buddhism and trade, encompassing nearby Topra Kalan where Emperor Ashoka erected the famous polished sandstone pillar with seven major edicts that Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq transported to Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi in 1356.

name: Buddhist Stupa Chaneti
description: Constructed in the 3rd century BCE during the Mauryan Empire by Emperor Ashoka, an ancient hemispherical Buddhist stupa built of concentric burnt bricks layered in mud mortar, identified with the monumental stupas described by 7th-century Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) at the ancient capital of Srughna (Sugh).

name: Ch. Devi Lal Herbal Nature Park Chuharpur
description: Spread across 184 lush acres in Chuharpur village near Bilaspur, developed by the Haryana Forest Department as a premier national herbal sanctuary conserving over 400 species of rare Ayurvedic, Unani, and Siddha medicinal trees and herbs, featuring an illuminated Navagraha Vatika, bamboo groves, medicinal nurseries, and a serene boating lake.

name: Chhachhrauli Fort & Kalsia State Heritage
description: The capital of the princely Sikh State of Kalsia founded in 1760 by Sardar Gurbaksh Singh, celebrated locally as the 'Cherrapunji of Haryana' due to recording the highest annual rainfall in the state, featuring the imposing 18th-century red-brick Chhachhrauli Fort with high circular bastions, clock tower, royal courthouse (Diwan-i-Am), and the picturesque Ravi Mahal.

name: Kalesar National Park & Forest Reserve
description: Covering 11,570 acres in the Shivalik foothills contiguous with Rajaji National Park (Uttarakhand) and Simbalbara National Park (Himachal Pradesh), the only dense natural Sal and Khair forest national park in Haryana, sheltering Asian wild elephants, leopards, sambar, barking deer, King Cobras, and the critically endangered Red Junglefowl.

name: Kapal Mochan & Rin Mochan Tirth Bilaspur
description: Situated 18 km from Jagadhri, an ancient pilgrimage centre with three sacred tanks (Kapal Mochan, Rin Mochan, and Suraj Kund) mentioned in the Mahabharata, where Lord Shiva cleansed himself of the sin of Brahma-hatya, where the Pandavas bathed after the Mahabharata war, and where Guru Gobind Singh Ji stayed for 52 days in 1688 after the Battle of Bhangani washing his warriors' weapons.
